text:
Ava R.: heads-up — I sketched a new synthetic generator for the kernel-selection benchmarks. goal: apples-to-apples between quantized kernels and fp16 kernels while exercising KV cache churn and batching heuristics.
Mike C.: nice. can you summarize the traffic shapes you want to run?
Ava R.: key shapes: 1) long ramp (0 -> peak over 10m) to exercise autoscaler, 2) cascade bursts (nested bursts with decaying amplitude) to force kernel handoffs, 3) microbursts (sub-second spikes) to measure tail latency, 4) heavy tail sampler that pushes 99.9/99.99 latency for end-to-end comparisons. also a replay harness mode where we feed recorded user QPS traces.
Sophia L.: for KV warmup, we should include a prefix-warm phase per session id. otherwise batching will look better than real. propose: 30s per session prefix walker that fills KV for top-k tokens.
Jordan P.: agree on prefix warm. also need a deterministic seed mode so we can rerun exactly and compare kernel-switch points. metadata must include model version, quantization profile, kernel id, and sequence length distribution.
Lee T.: what about batching heuristics? current runtime switches to group-batched kernels at 8 concurrent sequences. we should test boundaries: 4, 8, 12, 16 and also simulated contention where grouping delays exceed latency SLO.
Ava R.: good call. config will sweep batch_threshold=[4,8,12,16], max_batch_delay_ms=[0,2,5,10]. also run with KV cache hit ratios target=[10%,30%,60%,90%].
Mike C.: can we capture internal perf counters at 100Hz and dump per-second aggregates? need kernel runtimes, memcpy times, queue-depth, and batch sizes. perf-bot: please add flamegraphs for any regression >5% in p99.
perf-bot: ack — instrumentation patch applied to the harness. auto-upload to s3://redwood-perf/runs/{{thread_ts}} on completion.
Sophia L.: putting a sample loadgen fragment here — this is what the cascade burst looks like:
```json
{
  "name": "cascade-burst",
  "stages": [
    {"duration_s": 30, "qps": 200},
    {"duration_s": 10, "qps": 800},
    {"duration_s": 5,  "qps": 2400},
    {"duration_s": 30, "qps": 100}
  ],
  "interarrival": "poisson",
  "session_prefix_warm": {"duration_s": 30, "coverage": 0.6}
}
```
Jordan P.: that cascade will cause kernel handoffs if the kernel selection threshold is conservative. we should also test a smoothed sawtooth with randomized jitter to avoid accidental scheduling alignment.
Lee T.: for apples-to-apples: pin the stubbed IO layer (disable background GC/eviction jitter), run identical batch heuristics, and only vary kernel implementation + quantization. otherwise the noise floor kills signal.
Ava R.: exactly. plan: 3 runs per experiment: baseline (fp16 kernels), quantized-fast, quantized-stable. each run = 3 repeats, same RNG seed, same replay trace when in replay mode. collect token-per-second, p50/p95/p99/p99.99 latencies, kernel-switch counts, batch-size histogram, and KV hit distribution.
Mike C.: how long for a single run? cascade + long ramp + tail sampler — sounds like 20–30m. budgetable. also suggest a short smoke (5m) pre-check that validates KV warmup and instrumentation.
Sophia L.: added the smoke pre-check. will emit a small summary msg: "smoke OK" or long log. sample smoke config: {"duration_s":300, "qps":150}.
perf-bot: first dry-run done: smoke OK. uploaded metrics to s3://redwood-perf/runs/4161237890/smoke.json
Jordan P.: when analyzing results, use quantile-diff plots (paired) and mark crossover points where quantized kernels start outperforming baseline by tokens/sec while not regressing tail beyond 2%.
Lee T.: important: also track memory pressure during cascade spikes — we saw a past regression where memcpy latency spiked when host mem hit 85%. add host_mem_pct to metrics.
Ava R.: noted. final ask: everyone add one guardrail hypothesis you want us to test (e.g., kernel X regresses p99 at batch sizes >12). I'll compile and put the run matrix in the runbook.
Mike C.: my guardrail: quantized-stable should never increase p99 by >10% versus fp16 on the long ramp.
Sophia L.: mine: KV warmup coverage <50% should not produce >15% increase in token cost due to cache misses.
Jordan P.: mine: kernel handoffs must be <3/min for steady-state after ramp.
Lee T.: mine: host_mem_pct must remain <80% during cascade bursts or we abort run.
Ava R.: thanks — I'll publish the runbook and schedule the first batch tomorrow 09:00 PT. will tag results here. :rocket:
